channel.title: MintWave Studio Blog
channel.description: Practical guides from the makers of Cable Calc, MultiTimer, Days Until, Daily Budget, Hatch Day, Sire & Dam and Endly.

item.title: What size breaker for a cable? Match the breaker to the cable (IEC 60364)
item.description: How to choose a circuit breaker for a cable: the Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz rule with worked examples for 2.5, 4 and 6 mm² copper, why a bigger breaker is dangerous, and when to size the cable up.

item.title: How much can I spend per day? Work out a daily budget in 5 steps
item.description: Work out how much you can spend per day: take your income, subtract bills and savings, divide by the days until payday. Includes a worked example and how to handle overspending and big costs.

item.title: Progesterone timing for dog breeding: when to mate after the LH surge
item.description: How progesterone testing finds a bitch's ovulation: the baseline, LH surge and ovulation values in ng/mL and nmol/L, and the best days to breed with natural, fresh, chilled and frozen semen.

item.title: Why didn't my eggs hatch? Causes by candling stage and fixes
item.description: Eggs not hatching? Find the cause by stage: clear eggs, early deaths, dead in shell and chicks that pip but do not hatch. Temperature, humidity, turning, egg handling and lockdown fixes.

item.title: Best before vs use by: what food date labels really mean
item.description: Use by is about safety, best before is about quality. Learn the difference, what to do with food past each date, how opening changes things and how to track expiry dates so less food is wasted.

item.title: How to time a whole dinner with several timers at once
item.description: One timer is never enough for a real meal. Learn to work backwards from serving time, label every timer, use stopwatches for resting and handle the alarm that always goes off at the wrong moment.

item.title: What to track in an endometriosis symptom diary (and what to bring to your appointment)
item.description: A practical guide to keeping an endometriosis symptom diary: which symptoms, pain scores and impacts are worth logging, how to keep it low effort on bad days, and how to turn it into something a doctor can use.

item.title: Voltage drop: why a cable that carries the current can still be too long
item.description: A cable can be safe for the current and still drop too much voltage over distance. See the IEC 60364 formula, a table of maximum lengths for 1.5 to 16 mm² copper, and four ways to fix a long run.
